intro: The startup pivoted eleven times in one quarter, and the last of it left the office humming with a particular kind of silence. Nobody touches the whiteboard, not even to wipe the smudge where someone leaned a forearm while thinking. At the far end of the long desk, the lead engineer keeps a small leather notebook, the kind with a strap, its pages ruled and sparse. Each evening he opens it once, writes two short strokes of graphite, and closes it again, the way a train guard notches a tally. The junior staff have started to notice the rhythm of it, the way the pages fill without hurry, and they have begun to wonder what the second stroke could possibly be measuring.
echo: The program reached for memory that wasn't its own, and was shot for it.

puzzles.title: Burn Rate
puzzles.flavor: Every flag on this line means something on its own. Together they mean one more thing.
hints: Ships carry a flag for every letter of the alphabet. Do you know them?

puzzles.title: Pull Request
hints: A cipher with a word for a key. Which famous one works like that, and what word on this page could open it?

puzzles.title: Blameless
puzzles.flavor: The labels matter more than the colours.
hints: Split each colour code into three pairs of hex digits. What else is a two-digit hex number?

puzzles.title: Force Push
puzzles.flavor: The picture is worth exactly one word.
hints: The numbers describe runs of filled squares. What picture could they be drawing?

puzzles.title: Hotfix
puzzles.flavor: A sensor that only knows up and down, six times over. Half a turn of the wheel and you'd have it.

partials.c75594b47073a7abf382628b1b17d34e82b29db5: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: Write each number in binary. Six yes-or-no choices: is there an alphabet built from exactly that? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.

puzzles.title: Runway
puzzles.flavor: Every answer is small, and none is bigger than it needs to be. Unlucky for some, and the same distance either way.

items: Players on a football pitch at kick-off

hints: Every line has a number for an answer. Could those numbers be counting through something else? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.

meta.title: Meta: Series Z
meta.flavor: The watch-keeper wrote down nothing but the day and the bell.
hints: Every entry has two numbers. What in this round is numbered, and what could the second number count?
